paragraphs: Abba Yose ben Yohanan of Yenot (or Yoni), a Tanna of the Tosefta.

At the end of [Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 2:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kilayim.2.4.3), Rabbi Lazar son of Rabbi Shimon and Abba Yose ben Yohanan of Yenoach give fifty cubits for a large field. [The Tosefta](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosefta_Kilayim.2.4) reads “Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon and Abba Yose Chanan of Yoni say”; Zuckermandel’s Tosefta reads “Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon and Abba Yose ben Chanun of Yani say.”

[Yevamot 53b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.53b.4) has Abba Yose ben Yohanan of Jerusalem speaking in the name of Rabbi Meir. Possibly the initials I-Y were written and became “of Jerusalem.” [Keritot 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.6b.4) teaches: while grinding he says, “Grind well,” according to Abba Yose ben Yohanan. Possibly he is Abba Yose ben Yohanan of Yoni.[^1]

notes.text: Kilayim gives Yenoach, the consulted Tosefta gives Yoni, and Yevamot reads “of Jerusalem” in the tradition from Rabbi Meir. Keritot has הדק, “grind,” where Hyman supplies הרק. The expansion of א״י and the link to the Keritot speaker are Hyman’s proposals. Compare [Heilprin’s notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1992&lang=en).
